score.rationale: This proposal is exceptionally well-defined and scores highly across all dimensions. It presents a crystal-clear problem statement, explaining that prior back-end work requires a UI layer to fulfill the core feature promise. The scope is meticulously defined, with explicit boundaries that separate the MVP from future work, ensuring a focused and achievable deliverable. Acceptance criteria are specific, measurable, and tied directly to automation (Playwright tests, visual diffs), making verification unambiguous. The technical plan is grounded in reality, referencing specific files, existing systems (EUI, PD-2 stores), potential risks (PD-2 output availability), and even hardware specifications. Finally, its lifecycle linkage is outstanding, explicitly connecting this unit of work (PD-4) to prior increments (PD-1/2/3), the parent feature (FR-11), and downstream verification needs (FR-9), demonstrating excellent traceability and project awareness.
